title: Valid Palindrome
prompt:
A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting to lowercase and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forwards and backwards.

Given a string `s`, return `true` if it is a palindrome.

**Example**: `"A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"` → `true`.

Converging two pointers — but each pointer must skip characters that don't count.

args: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

hints: Inside the `while (l < r)` loop, first advance l past non-alphanumerics, then retreat r the same way.

solution.explanation: Insight: a palindrome check only needs to compare mirrored positions, so pointers from both ends that skip non-alphanumerics compare exactly the filtered characters. Each character is visited at most once by one pointer, and a single mismatch proves it isn't a palindrome. O(n) time, O(1) space — no cleaned copy needed; the inner skip-loops keep `l < r` so the pointers can't cross mid-skip.
